distinguishing_features: Applies ultrasonic impact treatment to the wheel-seat fillet to induce a compressive residual stress field, i.e., a physical mitigation rather than a monitoring/prediction scheme
Reduces effective stress intensity factor range by residual-stress superposition rather than by detecting damage from existing signals
Targets subsurface/crack-initiation-site mechanical state via surface treatment, not thermodynamic or vibration inference
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to suppress or delay fatigue crack initiation at a high-stress-gradient wheel-seat fillet without altering the axle geometry.
parsed.viable_reason: Ultrasonic impact treatment inducing 400-600 MPa compressive residual stress at a fillet is a physically established, testable mechanism measurable by XRD, and the proposed test with a numeric pass/kill condition is feasible at the stated scale.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: None of the prior art employs a mechanical surface-treatment mitigation; all three closest references are signal-inference monitoring schemes, so applying residual-stress engineering to close the initiation site is not an obvious extension of their approach.
